elements.quote: Specific objectives of the systemic review To determine the role of age in AT efficacy. To identify the optimal age for AT treatment. To examine whether the reported outcomes differ between age groups in children with Polysomnography (PSG)-confirmed uncomplicated OSA. To provide evidence-based suggestions for precise AT treatment in childhood.
elements.reason: The review explicitly states its objectives in the text, clearly outlining the goals regarding age, AT efficacy, and treatment outcomes.

elements.quote: Objectives : To assess the safety and efficacy of adenotonsillectomy (AT) for treating uncomplicated pediatric obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) in children of different ages.
elements.reason: The review defines the intervention (adenotonsillectomy), the population (children with uncomplicated OSA), and the outcomes (safety and efficacy) in the abstract, which functions as a PICO-style statement of the review's scope.

elements.quote: Studies were included if they met the following criteria: pediatric patients (<18 years) diagnosed with OSA using PSG based on widely accepted diagnostic guidelines at the time of publication and quantitative data available for outcomes of interest before and after surgery. In addition, the study should be published in English, and the study design should be case-control, cohort, randomized controlled trials (RCTs), or before-after studies.
elements.reason: The review specifies the population (pediatric patients <18 years with OSA), the diagnostic method (PSG), the study designs (case-control, cohort, RCTs, before-after), and the requirement for quantitative data.

elements.quote: In addition, the study should be published in English
elements.reason: The review specifies the language requirement (English) but fails to specify eligibility criteria regarding dissemination year or publication/report status.
The review does not distinguish between exclusion due to outcomes not being measured versus exclusion due to outcomes not being reported.

elements.quote: To understand the effect of age on AT outcomes, participants were grouped into multiple age thresholds according to study-reported means of 0-5 vs. >5, 0-6 vs. >6, 0-7 vs. >7, and 0-8 vs. >8 years.

elements.quote: Studies were excluded if they focused exclusively on complicated pediatric populations, such as those with comorbidities that could independently affect post-operative outcomes.
